Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your turn is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

 * own `{...props}` placement (spread last) — so a caller-supplied `color` or `to` is silently
 * overridden here instead of taking precedence, unlike those three siblings. This is a verbatim,
 * byte-for-byte port of the base file per SFCC-270's zero-functional-diff scope (plan step 2.1);
 * addressing it, if warranted, belongs to a later step (2.2), not this one.

 * `Link` is not overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing at time of
 * writing), so it stays on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path.

import React from 'react';
import { useItemVariant } from '.';
import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
import { Heading } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';

/**
 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this components simply renders
 * the item's name using the cart item field `productName`. We use this field
 * rather than variant `name` field as the variant detail may not yet be
 * available upon rendering.
 */
const ItemName = (props: Record<string, any>) => {
  const variant = useItemVariant();
  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;

  return (
    <Heading as="h2" fontSize="md">
      <Link {...props} color="black.600" to={`/product/${productId}`}>
        {variant.productName || variant.name}
      </Link>
    </Heading>
  );
};

export default ItemName;

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): Option B — override `item-variant/*` as well. 8 files.**
`product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}` +
`item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}`, all to `.tsx`.

Verified before deciding: **every consumer of `item-variant/*` is base/OOTB with no Zimmermann
design or development**, so brand styling landing on them is an upgrade toward Zimmermann, not a
regression from it. Full consumer list — `components/order-summary` (no override),
`components/multiship/multiship-order-summary`, `pages/account/order-detail` (account has zero
overrides), `pages/account/wishlist/partials/wishlist-primary-action` +
`wishlist-secondary-button-group` (and wishlist is migrating to `ZimmProductCard` anyway),
`pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group` (base cart page, replaced by the drawer),
`pages/checkout/partials/{pickup-address,product-shipping-address-card,shipping-product-cards}`
(checkout override is only `payment.tsx`), `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-product-shipping-address-card`.

**`pages/confirmation` is NOT in the blast radius** — `overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx`
already exists and does not use `item-variant`, so the base confirmation page is shadowed and never
renders. That was the one surface worth worrying about (a shopper sees it after paying).

**Two requirements for the override, both load-bearing:**
1. **Keep the defaults-then-spread order.** Callers set their own geometry —
   `order-summary` does `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` — and must keep winning.
   Write `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse, or you break layouts that work
   today. `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` already have it right.
2. **Fix `item-name` while in there.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread
   *before* the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after; no base caller
   passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.

**Deferred consequence, accepted:** when checkout is designed it will inherit cart-derived
line-item styling it never specified. Whoever picks up checkout should know why it already looks
part-branded.

**Governance:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/` is **Tier 2, Squad B-owned (notify Squad A)**
per `protectedFiles.md`. CODEOWNERS will request Squad B's review on a Squad A ticket.

**Interim consequence, low risk:** while the account wishlist page still consumes `product-item`, our
override's styling reaches it too. `overrides/app/pages/` contains no account pages at all — account
is entirely base and unstyled today — so the exposure is minimal until the wishlist migration lands.

### SFCC-271 — Quantity Stepper · 4 ACs · all buildable

ACs: `+` increments by 1 with item total and order summary updating; `–` decrements when quantity > 1;
at quantity 1 the `–` is disabled and quantity stays 1; drawer count (`Bag 3`) and order summary both
update without a full page load.

input.message: SFCC-270 review — angles: structure conventions, imports, accessibility, intra-step DRY. All 11 files read directly; findings below are grounded in that reading plus the greps/git history shown per-finding. I did not run tsc/vitest/storybook or a live render — those are other agents' lanes; anything requiring runtime confirmation is marked PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED. === TASK 1 — STRUCTURE === **1a. Default export (no named-export split) — CONFIRMED CORRECT, not a violation. 🔵 informational, ONE-OFF (applies uniformly, but as a "checked and clean" result, not a defect).** `overrideStyling.md`'s SFCC bridge-pattern section requires a named-export split (`CardBaseline`-style) only when styling forces a *structural* prop-surface change; it explicitly says token-driven theming "doesn't require a second export." All 5 components (`product-item/index.tsx:206`, `item-image.tsx:130`, `item-name.tsx:63`, `item-attributes.tsx:262`, `item-price.tsx:147`) style purely through the new co-located `.css.ts` recipes (`useMultiStyleConfig`/`sx`/`__css`), and every prop-surface change is additive-only with a default that preserves existing-caller behaviour: - `product-item/index.tsx:94-102` keeps even *unused* base PropTypes (`onAddItemToCart`, `isWishlistItem`) purely to stay API-compatible — direct evidence of deliberate bridge-pattern compliance. - `item-attributes.tsx:60,72`: `combineAttributeValues?: boolean` defaults to `false`, so every existing consumer (order-summary, multiship-order-summary, account/order-detail, wishlist partials, checkout partials — per `.claude/session-notes.md:345-351`'s consumer map) sees zero behaviour change. This is additive extension, not the kind of prop-*narrowing* (CardBaseline's `price` becoming a pre-rendered node) the carve-out is guarding against. - `session-notes.md:335-337` independently records the same conclusion at plan time ("put brand styling in a theme recipe, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second export CardBaseline's prop-narrowing did"). Also: none of the 5 are "default exports of anonymous functions" (components.md's literal wording) — all are named `const`s exported as default. Also not a default-export-vs-named-export issue under `components.md`'s general rule at all, since that rule targets new Zimmermann-authored (camelCase) components; these are override files mirroring base kebab-case SFCC files, where `overrideStyling.md`'s bridge-pattern rules govern instead. **Conclusion: single default export is correct here, no fix needed.** **1b. `item-name.tsx` missing `ItemNameProps` type — CONFIRMED pre-existing, out of this commit's scope. 🔵 note, ONE-OFF.** `item-name.tsx:50`: `const ItemName = (props: Record) => {` — no declared `Props` type, unlike its 4 siblings (`ItemImageProps` item-image.tsx:42-45, `ItemAttributesProps` item-attributes.tsx:54-61, `ItemPriceProps`/`PricePerItemProps` item-price.tsx:46-56,71-75, `ProductItemProps` product-item/index.tsx:88-106). Verified via `git show 22ca34c9:overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-name.tsx`: the identical `const ItemName = (props: Record) => {` signature line already existed in the prior copy-first commit. `git diff HEAD -- .../item-name.tsx` confirms this commit's diff touches only the docblock and the two JSX lines in the return (`textStyle`/`color` changes) — the signature line itself is untouched. **This gap pre-dates SFCC-270 step 2.2 entirely (inherited from step 2.1's copy-first port) and is out of this commit's scope** — worth a separate cleanup, not a defect in this diff. **1c. Missing individual stories for item-image/item-name/item-attributes/item-price — CONFIRMED gap, should-fix. 🟡, UNIFORM (recurs across all 4 sibling files).** `components.md` requires a story for "any component exported from its folder... i.e. anything another file imports," exempting only "purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent." Per `session-notes.md:307-314,345-351`'s consumer map, these 4 are consumed well beyond `product-item`: `order-summary`, `multiship-order-summary`, `pages/account/order-detail`, wishlist partials, checkout partials (`pickup-address`, `product-shipping-address-card`, `shipping-product-cards`, `one-click-product-shipping-address-card`) — i.e. they are not the single-parent-internal case the exemption describes. Checked the requested precedent: `overrides/app/components/header/leftBar/` and `header/rightBar/` **both have their own `index.stories.tsx` and `index.test.tsx`**, confirmed via `find`. Confirmed via `header/index.tsx:20-21` that `LeftBar`/`RightBar` are imported *only* by `header/index.tsx` — i.e. these are the single-parent-internal case, and this codebase **still** stories/tests them individually. That's a stronger, real precedent *against* skipping stories here — item-image/item-name/item-attributes/item-price have genuine multi-consumer status (unlike leftBar/rightBar) and still got no stories of their own. Only `product-item/index.stories.tsx` was added; `find overrides/app/components/item-variant -type f` shows zero `.stories.tsx` files anywhere in that folder. **Should-fix, not established practice.** **1d. `combineAttributeValues=false` (default/pre-existing per-key) branch is untested anywhere in this diff — CONFIRMED, real regression-risk gap. 🔴, shares root cause with 1e (see below).** `item-attributes.tsx:147-157` now has two mutually exclusive branches gated on `combineAttributeValues` (new, defaults `false` at line 72). `product-item/index.tsx:148` hardcodes `` — JSX shorthand for `combineAttributeValues={true}` — so `ProductItem` **only ever exercises the new combined branch, never the pre-existing default/per-key branch**. Searched exhaustively for any test of the `false` branch: - `item-attributes.tsx` has no test file of its own at all. - `item-variant/index.test.tsx` (116 lines, read in full) has exactly two `describe` blocks — `CartItemVariantImage (item-image)` (line 69) and `CartItemVariantName (item-name)` (line 91) — **no `CartItemVariantAttributes` coverage whatsoever**, combined or per-key. - `product-item/index.test.tsx` mocks `getDisplayVariationValues` (lines 66-72) and asserts only `screen.getByText('Lilac Sand, One size')` (line 155) — the combined-string branch — and can't reach the `false` branch at all since `ProductItem` never passes it. Net result: **the per-key rendering path — which is what every other real consumer (order-summary, multiship-order-summary, account/order-detail, wishlist partials, checkout partials) actually uses today — has zero test coverage anywhere in this diff**, despite `item-attributes.tsx` being modified in this exact commit to add the branching that guards it. This is precisely the pattern `testing.md`'s opening paragraph warns against relying on transitive/parent coverage instead of a component's own contract test. Flagging plainly per the brief's instruction. **1e. `item-price.tsx` has zero dedicated test coverage of its own — CONFIRMED gap, should-fix. 🟡, UNIFORM with 1d (same root cause: `item-variant/index.test.tsx` only covers 2 of 4 siblings).** `item-variant/index.test.tsx` has no `CartItemVariantPrice`/`item-price` describe block at all — confirmed by reading the full file. `product-item/index.test.tsx:151` asserts only that `'$495.00'` appears in the document (an incidental transitive string match).
